app.name: GitHub
app.managed_alternative_note: Composio provides one-click managed auth for GitHub. You do not need to register your own OAuth app unless you require custom white-label branding on the authorization prompt or enterprise organization-level policies.
when_to_byoc: Custom white-label branding: Display your own verified company organization and avatar on the consent screen
GitHub Enterprise Server: Direct OAuth integration with self-hosted on-premises GitHub Enterprise instances
Organization SSO policies: Compliance with internal enterprise IP allowlisting or SAML SSO enforcement

summary: Instant self-serve setup with zero review wait. Best baseline app for AI agents needing repo or issue access.
difficulty_factors: +0 pts: No mandatory review required for developer/internal usage
+0 pts: Free developer tier includes full OAuth app capabilities
+0 pts: Instant self-serve client ID and secret generation

time_estimate.production_wait_claim: Instant (no approval required for direct multi-user OAuth)

prerequisites: A free or paid GitHub account
A designated callback URL (e.g. https://your-agent.com/api/auth/callback/github or http://localhost:3000 for local dev)
Organization admin permissions if creating an organization-owned OAuth App

path.action: Navigate to Developer Settings in GitHub
path.detail: Go to GitHub Settings -> Developer Settings -> OAuth Apps -> Click 'New OAuth App'.

path.action: Fill out Application Name & Homepage URL
path.detail: Provide Application name (e.g. 'My AI Coding Agent'), Homepage URL, and optional description.
Enter the exact callback URL. GitHub supports wildcard paths only in limited enterprise cases; exact matching is recommended.
Click 'Generate a new client secret'. Store it immediately in your agent's secret store (.env). It will never be shown again.

path.action: Implement OAuth Code Exchange with Scopes
path.detail: Direct users to https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize with requested scopes (e.g. repo, read:user), exchange the code at https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token.

scopes.unlocks: Read profile information and public email
Grants full control of private repositories, issues, pull requests, and commit statuses

approval.what_reviewed: No review process exists for standard OAuth apps. Only GitHub Marketplace apps require review.
typical_rejection_reasons: OAuth apps are never rejected by GitHub staff because there is no review gate
Organization owners may block third-party OAuth apps via Org Settings -> Third-party application access restrictions
what_to_prepare: Valid callback URL with HTTPS (HTTP allowed only for localhost)

blockers_and_fixes.symptom: User sees 'Access denied by organization owner' when connecting an enterprise or team repo
blockers_and_fixes.cause: The target GitHub organization has OAuth app access restrictions enabled (default in most security-conscious orgs).
blockers_and_fixes.fix: Instruct the user to click 'Request approval' in the authorization dialog, or have an Org Admin navigate to Organization Settings -> Third-party Access -> Approve the app.
blockers_and_fixes.escalation_template: Hello [Org Admin], our team is integrating [Agent Name] to assist with repository automation. Could you please grant third-party OAuth approval for application client ID [CLIENT_ID] under Organization Settings -> Third-party Access?

blockers_and_fixes.cause: The redirect_uri passed in the authorization request does not exactly match the callback URL configured in Developer Settings.
blockers_and_fixes.fix: Ensure exact protocol (https vs http), port, and trailing slash match what is in GitHub Developer Settings.

agent_can_do: Draft OAuth route handlers and PKCE code challenge generation
Format GitHub API requests and handle rate limit backoff headers
Prepare scope request URLs based on required actions (issues vs code)
Validate webhook payloads using HMAC SHA256 secrets
you_must_do: Log into GitHub with your personal or organization account
Click 'New OAuth App' and copy the client secret into your environment vault
Approve organization access if accessing private corporate repos
agent_vs_human.handoff_critical_point: Human must create the OAuth App in GitHub Developer Settings and copy the Client ID and Secret to .env.

what_to_do_next: Open GitHub Developer Settings (https://github.com/settings/developers) and create the app.
Copy Client ID and generated Secret into your agent environment variables.
Test the local callback flow with 'read:user' scope.

evidence.claim: GitHub OAuth apps require zero review or approval to start issuing tokens to users
evidence.snippet: Anyone can create an OAuth app. When you create an OAuth app, you register it with GitHub and receive a client ID and client secret. You can distribute this app without submitting it for review unless listing on GitHub Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Exact callback URL match is required, though localhost allows custom ports
evidence.snippet: The redirect_uri parameter must match the registered callback URL. For localhost development, subdomains and loopback IPs are supported.

uncertainties: GitHub is transitioning toward fine-grained GitHub Apps with specific repository permissions over classic OAuth Apps; classic OAuth apps remain fully supported but GitHub recommends GitHub Apps for enterprise granular permissions.
